15:10 Local Time, 05:10 GMT, 10:40 IST: Just 159 runs in both innings combined from Bangladesh - a disappointing effort after what they achieved in Darwin. They've been blown away well inside two days, with Mitchell Starc the wrecker-in-chief, taking 10 wickets in the Test, six in the first innings and four in the second. This pitch in Mackay had more pace and bounce on offer than what we saw in the first Test, and the conditions were much more to Australia's liking. They also didn't make the mistake of batting first after winning the toss this time. Cummins inserted Bangladesh in and they were rolled over for just 64 yesterday morning. Australia weren't the most convincing with the bat either, but they still managed to secure a 146-run lead which was more than enough for the visitors who capitulated once more.

A tour on which Bangladesh achieved their greatest-ever win since making their international debut in 1986 has ended on a bitter note for them. Their batting was found out in conditions with more pace and bounce as Australia bounced back in style here in Mackay. But these last couple of weeks have confirmed the potential of Bangladesh's bowling attack. Even without Nahid Rana, the seamers made a big impact while Mehidy also had a say in conditions not ideally suited for him. Australia, on the other hand, went through a lot of scrutiny after the result in Darwin and question marks continue to linger over that batting lineup. They continue to lead the table in the World Test Championship but have a challenging run of fixtures in the next few months. First up will be the tour to South Africa, then New Zealand at home and then India away. A lot can happen during this time and Bangladesh are right in the mix when it comes to challenging for a spot in the top two. Exciting times ahead...
